utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Oric. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen, yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, please sit down. And Mr. Wubben, appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours and also good afternoon to the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, my name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts, and I wish to bid good day to my learned colleagues from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic and good afternoon to you and your team. Any preliminaries? None? Later on in the day, probably almost most definitely before 4.00 or before the Registry closes its doors, we will file the Rule 68 decision. All right? Any -- I hear you have no preliminaries? I have seen your lists of proposed list of documents. Is that indicative that you will probably finish your cross-examination by the end of business tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm certainly planning to. As I stated yesterday, that's my plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Because if you think that is no longer feasible, I will give instructions to Madam Registrar to contact the Victims and Witnesses Section to start preparing for alternative arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't think you need be alarmed by that list. I may even not use that. I do that to actually cover myself just in case I want to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As you see, Mr. Di Fazio and Mr. Jones, and the rest, we use our discretion. We distinguish between one witness and the other, and put our foot down where we need to. Otherwise, we don't. So let's bring the witness in, please. He may have gone home already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: SIDIK ADEMOVIC: [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Ademovic. I hope the earphones are in good functioning order and that you are receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Thank you. Yes. I am receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your testimony will continue very soon, and it is always in terms of the solemn declaration that you made before you started giving evidence on the first day. I'm just reminding you of that. Ms. Vidovic will finish with her examination-in-chief. She is going to do her utmost to finish the earliest possible and then Mr. Di Fazio will take you up for cross-examination and hopefully finish by tomorrow. Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ademovic, as you heard we are pressed for time and I ask you wherever possible to answer request a yes or no or just with a brief answer, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance in showing the witness a document by the command of the Drina Corps, a new document which is called "request for assistance and engagement of appropriate unit." This is a Drina Corps command document addressed to the commander of the eastern Bosnia corps bearing the following number, 04293309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While this is being distributed, Madam Vidovic and Mr. Wubben, and the rest of the staff, we have succeeded in moving tomorrow's sitting from the afternoon to the morning. I just received a confirmation of it now. I take it that -- I mean, I gave instructions that this is only confirmed after that I have the consent of everybody. So I'm just informing you that tomorrow morning, we will have a sitting from 9.00 until quarter to 2.00 rather than in the afternoon. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Your question, Ms. Vidovic. The document has been distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, please look at the date of the document, 26th of December 1992. I will quote a small portion of the document. In the first part of the document, it is stated, "Please help us physically defend Bratunac town by engaging your unit under Mauzer's command. We believe that the engagement of his unit would be most effectively carried out along the Milici-Rogac-Lipenovici-Martinci-Kravica-Bratunac operation axis. By using this axis we would achieve the following. We would separate the enemy forces of Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje. We would surround the enemy forces in the Glogova mountain sector, Halilovici and Velika Glogova villages and we would lift the blockade of Bratunac town to the west." Here is my brief question for you. The axis described herein the Milici-Rogac-Lipenovici-Martinci-Kravica-Bratunac axis, how far apart is that from Bratunac, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15 kilometres is Kravica, Kravica, and the Milici-Rogac-Lipenovici-Martinci some 20 kilometres away from Bratunac. However, the entire area is contiguous to the area under my control.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Lipenovici-Martinci-Kravica, have I understood you well? You meant that these were the villages that neighboured your territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In late December 1992, did you find out about the arrival of new, fresh Serbian forces from different directions to the area of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Over my Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn about the arrival of Mauzer and perhaps some other units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mauzer and Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Madam Vidovic, this document will become Defence Exhibit D853. It consists of one page in B/C/S with ERN 04293309, and two pages in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to correct the transcript. The witness said "Yes, the arrival of Mauzer, and Krajisniks." That can be found 14.34.14. Is that the eighth line? The 8th line, 14.34.14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was, "Did you learn about the arrival of Mauzer and perhaps some other units?", and the answer as it appears on the transcript says "Yes, Mauzer and Krajisnik." What did you -- something wrong here, it seems. What did you answer to that question, Mr. Ademovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mauzer and units of the Krajina men, therefore units from the Krajina area, Western Bosnia. The part around Banja Luka to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was necessary because Krajisnik has got different connotations inside the four walls of this Tribunal. Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you could the usher please show the witness the document by the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army dated 5 January 1993? The document was signed by the assistant commander for logistics, Major General Djordje Djukic bearing the number 04261922. I will briefly quote from the document. "The Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska," and it says "sent to the Drina Corps command." "By monitoring the conception of ammunition from your daily logistics reports of 1st January 1993, 2nd January, and 3rd January 1993, we have established that on these three days, you used enormous quantities of certain types of ammunition. For example, consumption of 7.6-millimetre bullets for automatic rifles alone was 256.000 in the above three days, in brackets, which is the equivalent of the total researches of this type in the 27th POB. In view of the situation with ammunition reserves at our disposal, such a rate of consumption is unsustainable. Serious attention should be paid to that." Mr. Ademovic, is it true or not that the Drina Corps covered the area of Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, in early January 1993, the three days mentioned in the document, namely 1st, 2nd and 3rd January, where were the combat activities of the Drina Corps focused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The areas of Susnjari, Brezevo Polje, Jaglici, Glogova, and the region of Krivic [phoen] Polje. You can see what the consumption of ammunition was and how high it was according to this document. For instance, the consumption of 7.6-millimetre bullets, this document refers to only one calibre, whereas at that period, we were being attacked by all types of weaponry available, infantry weapons, artillery, and aviation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness the 256.000 bullets only refer to the ammunition of the automatic rifles, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and only to the 1-calibre type of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be assigned a number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document will become Defence Exhibit D854, consists of two pages, one in English, one in Serbo-Croat, reference number ERN number 04261922.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this, Mr. Ademovic, I will ask you as follows: Is it not true that the Serbs in this particular period, and I'm referring to this several days in early January, were carrying out an extensive offensive in the entire area of Susnjari, Bret -- Cizic [phoen] Polje, Jaglici and Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your personal reaction to that? I mean you personally. And those who were with you in Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got in touch with the leaders of my groups and I deployed my men wherever I could in order for them to let everyone know what was in store for us that we were practically going to be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to clarify one matter. Here it is stated "I got in touch with the leaders of my groups." Which groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The groups that were nearby in Jaglici and Brezova Njiva. Those were the areas under my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "my groups," does it mean that they fell under your command or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In my area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're referring to the adjacent groups to yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Jaglici and Brezova Njiva.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was going on during the night between the 6th and the 7th January 1993 or were you able to listen in to the Serbian communications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the afternoon on the 6th and in the course of the night between the 6th and the 7th as I was listening into their communications I realised that they were preparing for a large-scale offensive and that the people in Glogova were in harm's way. According to the information I heard, the thrust of the attack was to be directed at Glogova from the direction of Bratunac, and Jelavci [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell you what -- tell us what you did next.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since some of the groups that were nearby were informed, we had the leaders of the group from Milacevici, Brosevici, and the adjacent group in Jaglici and Brezova Njiva arriving to our aid. They realised that unless something is done, we are going to be wiped out. New refugees were imminent and that is why we decided that we should do something about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who took this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of us, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you set out in some direction and where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Across Djermani towards Jezestica, not because it was Christmas and because these religious holidays were not to be respected but for different reasons, namely we knew that on that particular day, they were going to be drunk and less careful. Another reason was that a column of several thousand refugees from Glogova were in danger of total extermination and also because in my region there were several thousand refugees who were starving. Therefore, the third reason was the food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, now you indicated the reasons behind such a decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did you set out in the direction of Jezestica and how many of you were there in the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we set out at about 10.00 and there were a total of around 50 of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were armed. We had nothing to lose. We would have died either way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At what time did you arrive in the area of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across to Djermani and into Stara Jezestica I arrived at around 10.00 and I saw --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure of the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where I saw a number of people who were fighting over a corn cob.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know where these civilians were from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stay while in Jezestica or did you move on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we moved on to Karici but it was difficult to advance because there was shooting still and, upon our arrival in Kajici, intense shelling started upon the entire area. We already came upon injured and wounded and even dead civilians. Some of my soldiers were also injured, and we could hardly advance because we will to take certain measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, let me ask you the following. The interpreter did not catch the time you mentioned as the time of arrival in Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At around 10.00, 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what time did you arrive in the area of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours, sometime after 12.00 p.m., because we were advancing slowly. I had several men who were wounded. And we were under intense shelling from the Serb forces from the direction of Rogac. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the shelling also directed at Kajici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've already stated that already in Kajici several of my men were wounded, some of them seriously, some lightly, and even some civilians were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the reason why you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That but also the -- because the approach road was very difficult to pass. It was in and around Kravica that the fighting was going on from all sorts of infantry weapons. Q. Upon Kravica or from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. From Kravica, from houses, from the school, from the warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. As far as I've understood what you were saying you did not go into Kravica, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us leave Kravica for a while. I want to turn to some other issues now. Is it not true that very soon you received information that you had to return to your area because of a counterattack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the men from my group remained at Ravni Buljim. That's the elevation point 820. From where -- which was constantly under attack from the area of Rogac. That was my area. That was constantly under artillery and infantry fire. And the attack against that area intensified.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the subsequent days after the 7th of January 1993, did you have any information to the effect that the civilians were leaving your area to go in the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they -- did some of them get killed over there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was intense shelling upon the civilians and many of them were massacred.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to prevent them from going there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Having been aware of what was going on there, and besides one could see that for himself, despite that, they were hungry, they could not be dissuaded and even if one tried to dissuade them, they stayed there, lingered on, and found different reasons why they had to go out in search of food. The most imminent reason being that they don't want to watch their children starve.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will go back to Kravica later on, if time will allow us. I just want to show you some documents now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness Prosecution Exhibit 290?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, P80.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the document by the staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica, 19 September 1993, and that's the delivery of the information on the breakdown of the formation structure of Srebrenica armed forces during the past period. And under item 1 it's stated on 20th May 1992, the Srebrenica TO staff was formed in Bajramovici. From 17 April 1992 to mid-October 1992 the first regional units were formed under the auspices of the TO of a regional character therefore. I would like to dwell on this for a while. Mr. Ademovic, first of all, in May 1992, were you aware of a meeting in Bajramovici where the Srebrenica TO staff was formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I've heard about this for the first time in Nijaz Masic's book or, rather, I read it there for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know whether some of the local group leaders from Jaglici and Brezova Njiva attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were my neighbours and I was in touch with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Until October 1992, in relation to your groups, did you use the term Territorial Defence on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. These were the groups or units, as people said later on. In essence they were groups of people from Susnjari, Jaglici. There was a group from Brezova Njiva, a group from Slatina, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked about these units among yourselves, how would you refer to other groups, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to say Zulfo's men, Sidik's men, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the period from the beginning of the war, until October 1992, were you active as part of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, independently, in my area of Susnjari, because I was physically cut off and it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The transcript reads "as part of Potocari." Did you understand me to mean were you part of any military formation, any part of a group in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from Potocari --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... because this only made it worse actually. When Madam Vidovic asked you the question in the period from the beginning of the war until October 1992, whether you were active as part of Potocari, what did you understand? What did you understand her to mean, to be asking you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the question to mean whether I was in the composition of Potocari, if I understood it properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that was what I asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But when you further asked about whether -- did you understand me to mean -- and he answered "no." So it had to be clarified because as it was, it could have -- I mean we would have understood it just the same but you never know whether we will still be here when the case is decided. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I hope you will.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you understood us to be discussing whether up to demilitarisation anyone from Potocari was your commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. What I've been saying all along is that I was independent and that I was not in the composition of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you write reports to anyone throughout 1992 and all the way up to the demilitarisation in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive orders or instructions from anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Throughout 1992, all the way up to the demilitarisation, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at this document, which reads, "TO Potocari." Look at some of the names on this list. For example, the Peciste company, "Peciste company," it says here, "Nasir Sabanovic, commander." I want to ask you the following: From the 20th of May 1992 until mid-October 1992, were there any companies on the ground in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There were only groups. There was no Peciste company. This village was depopulated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Nasir Sabanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says here "commander." He was never a commander. I know him well from peace time. He's from a place called Podcaus in Bratunac and for two or three months he was a refugee in Caus in the Sase and Bratunac area. He couldn't have been a commander. And this did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A little lower down it says, Budak company, commander Ibrahim Mandzic. Before October 1992, did Budak have any kind of corporal makes. Explain to Their Honours where it is and what it is, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Budak is physically adjacent to Bratunac at the exit point of Bratunac. And in that period of time, there were no people there because every house had been leveled to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at what it says Susnjari company. It says 59 military conscripts. How do you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were not that many women or children, let alone men, in my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And were there any refugees in your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was a voluntary group. As I said, my group had 25 lads. As for this number here, 95, well, I can't tell lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up to October 1992, were you under the command of Naser Oric whom you know well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was independent, a group leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, did you have areas of responsibility in the military sense of the word, established on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't know about areas of responsibility in the military sense. We didn't even know what this was about. We each had our territorial area where we were active, as I was in the area of Susnjari, Jaglici, and Brezova Njiva. However, the military sense of the word area of responsibility is something else. I think Their Honours know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document then contain correct information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is quite contrary to the truth, to reality, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You -- we mentioned demilitarisation. Can you explain what this meant for your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Demilitarisation in the true sense of the word, means the cessation of all activities having to do with combat activities or any other military activities. For my group, demilitarisation meant the cessation of all activities and all 25 of my lads, including myself, we all handed in our weapons as required by the UN representatives who had come into my terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did the activity of the army consist of? What was it reduced to in these conditions of demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only filling in forms on paper, relating to military conscripts, and other kinds of information. There was nothing active going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Excuse me, if Your Honours please, what army is the witness referring to? It's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you think it needs clarification, Madam Vidovic can address that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said -- replied, Your Honour, but it's not in the record. I think he was referring to Tuzla, and it could be heard. I will repeat the question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To what were the activities of what remained under demilitarisation after demilitarisation reduced? And you mentioned Tuzla. Could you repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was reduced to listing military-able men, making lists, putting people on lists. These were technical, administrative matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, I do need a confirmation from him that he had mentioned Tuzla before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are not following in B/C/S like I am not following in B/C/S. That's why I want a confirmation, because it has been suggested by Ms. Vidovic and I have no reason to doubt her word but I do want a confirmation from him. After the demilitarisation, which army are we talking about? Or you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what you understood me to say. It wasn't an army. It was a list of military-able men. Their names were put down on paper, on paper. These were technical matters. Putting down on paper. It was nothing to do with an army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see now what led to the confusion. I in fact asked what military activities were taking place after the demilitarisation. My question was misinterpreted. What activities of troops, soldiers, army happened? My question was misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what were the remaining military activities, if any, on the ground? That's what evidently led to confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood you quite well, and that's what I replied. Technical matters. No military activities. In the military sense, a list of military-able men. That is administration, no military activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But did you at any time mention Tuzla in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In which context? This is what we need to know so that we close this chapter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were these technical matters that were ordered after the demilitarisation, to put on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And where did these instructions come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Tuzla. From Tuzla because they didn't accept us as legal soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suggest that during the break, Mr. Di Fazio and I listen to the recording, part of the recording, and you will hear what -- that what I have just described was said. And the witness has repeated it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If Mr. Di Fazio is interested in that, because I don't think we are interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- with all due respect to Madam Vidovic, I think everything has been explained to me and I'll deal with this in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, did you know of the existence of a Paket connection with Tuzla when you arrived in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I learned about it when I came to Srebrenica and that's precisely what this related to, what I've just said, the Paket communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about an order to form the 8th operations group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have not heard of such an order. Have you heard of the formation of a large military unit in early 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about it but it only dealt with technical matters. It was just putting down on paper. They insisted that we put these units down on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you are trying to say is that it did not exist on the ground but only on paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I've been saying all along. After the demilitarisation, there was nothing on the ground. It was all only on paper, because they refused to accept us as legal members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So we had to deal with these technical matters on paper. There was no activity on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir. Did you become a member of some such unit on paper, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The 280th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you assigned some kind of duty at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that I had been assigned some kind of duty but I never received any document concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What duty was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Allegedly they said I was assistant commander for security and then assistant to the commander for morale but I was never that. I've never even saw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, just a clarification that I suggest needs to be made for you to understand this evidence - excuse me - that the witness said "they refused to accept us as legal members of the army of" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, I don't know if it's clear to you. It's not clear to me whether the witness is referring to "they" as being the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I think it's important to know because this is what this whole issue turns on, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand it like that. But perhaps you can put the question direct to the witness so that he can answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did not want to accept you as legal members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In those documents and instructions, that arrived in -- from Tuzla through those Paket communications, if we did not fill in those forms, they would not accept us and recognise us as members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina because we were physically cut off from them and not connected to them, and they sent those instructions through those communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will now look at a specific document which will clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall clarify this through two documents and I think it will become clear then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in listing those units on paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you put down that group on paper, what did you personally call it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I called it the Susnjari unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened after that? Let's take it step by step. So you write it down, and you send it through Paket communications to Tuzla, and you write down Susnjari unit. What happens in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Tuzla they reject that name for the unit and they say that the units are not to be listed by village. Instead, they send us instructions that we have to use military terminology to name the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness a document? This is a document by the 2nd Corps command of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated 24th of February 1994, bearing the following title: "Appointments and proposals for appointments. Warning." Below one can see that it was delivered to the 8th OG and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will quote item 3 of the document. The telegram is signed by a commander, Brigadier Hazim Sadic. First of all I want to ask you the following. Do you know who Hazim Sadic was in 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was commander of the 2nd Corps based in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In connection with this, I will read out item 3 of the document. And I quote: "In the future, no appointment proposal shall be taken into consideration if it is not in accordance with the temporary war formations which means that you must urgently restructure all non-formation compositions and positions, and fit them within the framework of the existing war formations." Are you familiar with the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this what you were referring to, that you adopted one thing and then those from Tuzla would instruct you that it was not possible, that this could not be called Susnjari unit but some -- that a military term should be used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, Your Honours, I told you that I wanted the unit to be called the Susnjari unit and they wrote back by saying that we should have a company, a platoon, a military term, and this is precisely what I had in mind when I was talking earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, is this the only such document that you set eyes on or did you perhaps receive several such documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We received several of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Having received these warnings from Tuzla, did you act in practice in compliance with these instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document will become Defence Exhibit D855. It consists of two pages, one in English and one B/C/S, and the ERN number is 01838420.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that the people from Srebrenica, after the demilitarisation, filled out applications for active military duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard something about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In filling out these forms, did the people have to comply with the instructions received from the 2nd Corps command and use military terms for the names of the units rather than their own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is precisely what we were discussing earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the usher to show another new exhibit to the witness. Could the witness be shown the document 01837831? This is a request for admission into the active military service with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document. Do you agree that I showed you this document during proofing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the part of the document bearing the signature. Did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the page bearing your signature, where it is stated, "The date of entry into service with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina." There is the official organ you applied to and you wrote 18th of March 1992, the date of establishment of the Susnjari unit. Did you write this down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was the day when I placed myself at the -- at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. 18th of March 1992, when the Susnjari unit was established and when I was chosen as its commander, and therefore the date I placed myself at the army's disposal, 18th of March -- 18th of April 1992. Can I ask you the following? Were you a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as of that date or were you recognised as its member at a later date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was not recognised as being a member as of that date because my unit, the Susnjari unit we referred to earlier on, was not recognised as such, and I had to sort the matter out retroactively, even through an administrative procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now that you mentioned the administrative procedure, is it not true that the people arriving from Srebrenica had to, after 1995, prove that they had participated in armed combat and that there were members of the army in large numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were thousands of such administrative procedures. Some of them are still pending today. I had to personally attest for each and every one of the members of my group, that they were members, active members, because we were not recognised as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please stop there. Can you look at this questionnaire? Did the military authorities accept this questionnaire as valid and admit you into the military service on the basis of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They did not accept the document bearing this particular title, and they did not admit me into service on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they ask you to draft another document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But I refused to do so and I was never a member of the army later on, and I was engaged in the business in which I'm engaged in to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You refused to do so because you wished to remain in the police; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the Witness P95?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We need to give this a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will become Defence Exhibit D856, and it consists of, in the B/C/S, pages starting with ERN number 01837831. Is it 8 or 6, the third number? I'm not quite sure whether it's 8 or 6. 8, according to the English translation, then, it's 8. Right through and inclusive of ERN 01837834. That's four pages, and the corresponding translation into English consisting of six pages. And that will be D856. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have the document before you. Please turn to page 6, to save time. This is allegedly a document by the 8th operations group command. Please turn to page 6. And you will see that this section has to do with the 280th East Bosnian Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is page 5 in the English text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next, please turn to page 9. Item 4, which in English is page 7. There are names of commanders and -- names of commanders and other senior officers since the formation until 31st January 1994, sixth line from the bottom in Bosnian, it is stated, "assistant commander for morale, in brigade from 2nd December 1992, to 10 January, 1994, Sidik Ademovic." Apart from you in the area was there another Sidik Ademovic who could be placed in connection with the 280th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please, or rather once again, it is stated here that the assistant commander for morale in the brigade from 2nd December 1992 to 10 January 1994, could you tell the Trial Chamber where were you on the 2nd of December 1992 and throughout December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my earlier testimony, the entire month of December and onwards, I was in the area of Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the fighting that took place at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that suffices.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was there a brigade in place at the time? Were you a member of a brigade on the 2nd of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the 2nd of December I had only that one group that I have been referring to throughout my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your career, were you ever an assistant to the commander for morale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is not really pertinent for the sort of business I'm involved in.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 11. It says "written commendation of the commander of the armed forces of Srebrenica for -- on the occasion of the first anniversary of the staff."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe the witness's answer was a bit different from the answer recorded here. Were you in your career ever an assistant to the commander? He stated that this would "not be compatible with the work that I do," and not perhaps "pertinent to the sort of business I'm involved with."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, tell us what did you really mean to say when you were answering my question whether ever in your career you were assistant to the commander for morale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never, never, because the sort of work I do is not related to that, and I never was an assistant commander for morale.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look -- turn to the middle of the page. Among the names of the persons, recipients of this certificate of merit, there is the name of Sidik Ademovic. Can you tell us whether you ever received a written certificate of merit from Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't receive a written or an oral credit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not even a verbal or a written or a pecuniary or any other sort of a credit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were a member of this 280th Brigade on paper in early 1994, and you were told that you were supposed to discharge the duties of the assistant commander for morale. Can you tell us what were you doing and where you were in the course of 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Demilitarisation meant rest for me. I was in my village of Susnjari, at home, at my parents' home, doing farm work. That was our only source of income.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness a new exhibit? This is a document by the command of the 8th operations group Srebrenica dated 9 September 1994. Weekly report by Nedzad Bektic. And the document bears the number 02103048.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please turn to page 2. And I will quote the words of Mr. Bektic according to this document, what is contained on page 2 under C. "The work of the commands and their cooperation is unsatisfactory. In the beginning of the week, an assessment of the security situation was sent to the 2nd Corps. The assessment was not done by organs of security. The command of the 282nd Brigade, the commander had left the duty wilfully and has not been discharging the duty for two months, without having been released and a new person appointed. "In the command of the 281st Brigade, the Chief of Staff, Zulfo Salihovic, has been working as the president of the SDA party since April. In the same Brigade, the assistant commander for morale, Abdic Hajrudin, resides in Srebrenica and appears in the unit only rarely, and he never comes to the meetings of the assistant commander for moral in the command. The assistant commander for security of 282nd Brigade, Abdul Jovic, and 281st Brigade, they have been furnishing incomplete reports, not reflecting the situation in the unit. They failed to produce and deliver a weekly report. The commander -- the assistant commander for morale, Sidik Ademovic," and so on and so forth. Is this your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. Madam Usher, just to -- wait, wait, just don't move anything. Is this the only part of there document that you have shown on the ELMO or did you show also the first page? Only this part. All right. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Before we continue, this document, which will become Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D857, will be preserved under seal. It consists of two pages in B/C/S -- sorry, three pages in B/C/S, and two pages in English, and with a sequential ERN number from 02103048 right flew and inclusive of ERN number 02103052. All right? Thank you. So Judge Eser has a question and Madam Registrar has a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, which has just been made use of with this witness, is going to become Defence Exhibit D857, and because of its contents, it will be kept and stored under seal. In consists of two pages -- three pages in B/C/S and two pages in English, all five pages are enumerated sequentially with ERN number 02103048 right through and inclusive of ERN 02103052. Yes, Judge Eser has a question -- I was going to say has a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: No, I have no problem. Just a matter of clarification of the language. I have realised that when you asked the witness a question or read from the exhibit, it was translated "assistant commander for morale," but if I go to the English translation, it speaks of "assistant commander for security." Now, in my understanding, morale and security are different things. Now, what is the meaning in B/C/S? Is it more in terms of morale or in terms of security?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, will you please tell me what part of the document you're referring to? Because Abdic Hajrudin, commander for morale is mentioned as well as Mr. Sidik Ademovic, commander for security. Which part of the document is Your Honour referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Referring to what you have just read. If you go to the English translation which is the ERN number which ends with 052, you ever assistant commander and it would say "for security."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the only line which has highlighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Yes. And the same with the other two persons you mentioned here. It doesn't speak of morale but security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, in the B/C/S it's on 3049 and the word is [B/C/S spoken] I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [B/C/S spoken]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. That's the word I think we are concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Exactly. What is the meaning of this B/C/S term [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is this. I think the point raised by my colleague Judge Eser is very valid because if you look at the same document a few lines before, with regard to Hajrudin Avdic, you will see that you will have [B/C/S spoken]. Further down, you have [B/C/S spoken]. So I take it that one means morale, the other one means security, as per the translation that we have. And very rightly. So perhaps an explanation is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just look at exactly what it says in the Bosnian version. This is a translation we received from the Prosecutor's office, and I have not had an opportunity to check it because we have only just received it. However, I will read out exactly what it says about Mr. Hajrudin Avdic: "In the same Brigade, the assistant commander for morale or moral guidance, Avdic, Hajrudin lives in Srebrenica and turns up in the unit very rarely. And as for meetings, at the assistant commandment -- commanders for the morale in the operations group, he hardly ever comes there. Assistants of the commander for security" - these are other people now - "of the 281st Brigade, Abdulah Ahmetovic, and the 282nd, Suad Smajlovic sent incomplete reports, thus covering up the real situation in the unit. The weekly report for this period has not been done by them or delivered." This is -- and then it says, assistant commander for security of the 280th, Sidik Ademovic. That's what it says in the original. "Assistant commander for security of the 280th, Abdulah Ahmetovic, assistant commander for security, Azmir Golic, of the SVB." That's what it says in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. It's -- the clarification that we need now is this: Was Sidik Ademovic, that's the witness, assistant ever -- ever assistant commander for morale, as has been suggested some time back, or was he actually or supposedly assistant commander for security, as seems to show -- as seems to appear from this document? This is basically what the clarification that we require because so far it has been suggested to the witness that he may or may not have been assistant commander for morale or moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I may be of some assistance, Your Honour, because the fact is, in P95 there is reference to assistant commander for morale and assistant commander for security. So there were two separate posts which the witness was asked about and which he answered. So the reference to morale before wasn't a mistake or an error. In this document it's simply security and I think will be -- that -- we can deal with that per this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with that? Oh, yes, let's go on then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please, I put the question to Mr. Ademovic very clearly, and Your Honours, with all due respect, I really sometimes cannot understand some questions of part of the Chamber. With all due respect, I asked Mr. Sidik Ademovic very clearly, "In your entire career, why you ever an assistant commander for morale?" He said "No." Then I moved on to another document which very clearly deals with what he's talking about now, that on paper he was the assistant commander for security. So believe me I myself am confused now and it's very hard for me to follow my own questions because the witness answered quite clearly and now this is confusing for me, let alone for the witness. Now I understand that Judge Eser is referring to two different documents. One document is something I've dealt with and the witness has clearly stated that never in his lifer was he an assistant commander for morale and now I have very important questions about this other document that we are dealing with now. I do respect the Court. I was a judge myself for 14 years. But sometimes I really need to say that I fail to understand Your Honour's questions. I do apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to make it clear, if you look to the transcript, page 29, line 4, it was within your question that you formulated, the commander, the assistant commander for morale, Sidik Ademovic, line 4, that's what I was referring to. It was your language, assistant commander for morale. You find it in the transcript, at least in the English one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- let's move because we need to finish. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry, I cannot follow the transcript. I do believe there are mistakes in the transcript. I cannot look at both the document and the transcript. But however that may be.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, we were discussing this document and now I will put a question in connection with it. If you look at the part on page 02103049, it says here "the work of the commands and cooperation with the commands is unsatisfactory," and the date of the document is the 9th of September 1994. Do you agree with what is stated in this document, that the work of the commands and cooperation with them during 1994 was unsatisfactory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fully agree, this is the time when there was demilitarisation and there was no work going on, and you could see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ademovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document goes on to say that, when evaluating the security situation, "the security organs did not participate, that some of them abandoned their posts, that the Chief of Staff of one brigade is working as a member of the SDA party, that Hajrudin Avdic, although he is an assistant commander for moral guidance, doesn't turn up in his unit or attend meetings." Does this document describe the actual situation in the alleged commands of these brigades and the 8th operations group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely so. There was nothing happening. There was no work going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that the assistant commanders for security are delivering incomplete reports and that you have failed to deliver a weekly report at all. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at what it says in the document below the date on the 9th of September 1994, "the municipal assembly of Srebrenica had on its agenda the political situation in the enclave and members of the SVB have not been invited to that meeting." Is the SVB the military security service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which illustrates the cooperation with civilian structures. It goes on to say "I would add that on the 8th of September 1994, I spoke with the president of the municipality, Mr. Osman Suljic requesting that this point be placed on the agenda and that I should be present but I was not invited." Please, do you agree that it follows from this document that the civilian organs even did not want to invite to their sessions security people or have contacts with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They neither invited them nor did they need to invite them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another question in connection with this: After the demilitarisation, did the military police exist and function properly in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was only the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P578? This is an enactment of the transitory municipal council of Srebrenica dated the 11th of March 1995. P578. I will quote one portion of the document. This is somewhere in the middle of the document. "After a couple of hours of analysis, we all unanimously concluded that the political security situation in the enclave was very complex and difficult, conditioned by a number of factors, but certainly the major factor that influenced the worsening of the situation was the incident caused by senior captain Ejub Golic, commander of the independent mountain Battalion. With the aim of overcoming the situation that can and should be overcome, we adopted a number of conclusions among which we would like to point out the following. Full support was given to our commander of the 28th division, Brigadier Naser Oric. Decision was taken to imprison and take Merdzic, Nezir [phoen] and Sadik Begic to the municipal prison which was already done." Have you heard about this incident.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the outcome of the incident was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the source of information for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Ejub Golic himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you? How did this incident end? Briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naser Oric took him to Tuzla to the 2nd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown another exhibit, which is a document by the district military court in Tuzla, number SU 106/95, dated 25th of April 1995. Security organ of the 2nd Corps, or rather "the district military court of Tuzla addresses the 2nd Corps command, to Colonel Mehmed Zilic and signed by Ismet Krumic." It says as follows: "On the 20th of March 1995, the Tuzla Security Services Centre informed us that the Srebrenica prison had come under an armed attack during which a number of individuals were helped to escape with the use of force. A group of some 20 members of the army were led by the commander of the independent Battalion, Ejub Golic. The CSB report also says that in late 1992, Ejub Golic murdered two people and was never held to account. There is also suspicion that in March 1995, he set on fire the flat of a Srebrenica judge, possibly because he was angry that some of "his men" had been remanded in custody. I have information that in the meantime Ejub Golic has moved to Tuzla and that he's still there. You are kindly requested to check the allegations from the above CSB report and to undertake measures within your competence and responsibilities." You've told us that you spoke to Golic. Can you tell us, please, when this was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon his return from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you whether the judicial authorities in Tuzla were informed of the criminal offences he allegedly perpetrated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what he told you, if so, did they talk to him about his alleged criminal offences in the command of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this document be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He needs to repeat his answer because the interpreter did not catch it. What was your answer, Mr. Ademovic, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was: Did they talk to him in the command of the 2nd Corps, or rather who talked to him, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They did. Commander Sead Delic and a certain Mehmed Zilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document, Madam Vidovic, will become Defence Exhibit D858, it consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, with ERN number 02622028.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness a new exhibit, which is an interview with General Sead Delic in the paper Dani. Delic-Dani, Oric left Srebrenica of his own will. It was published on the 7th of March 2000. Witness, please turn to page 3 of this document. That's page 3 of 8, and Your Honours in English, that's page 2 in the middle of the page. The interview was taken by Vildana Selimbegovic. The question by the journalist was, "Dani: Perhaps, but the time of schooling is quite controversial. Besides that is one of the questions that the military leadership has failed to answer. Delic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. answers: I can only state my opinion. Brigade commanders were not in that group. As far as I know, Naser came of his own accord. No one had invited him. I know for sure that late Ejub Golic, commander of a battalion, also came with them (died in the breakthrough through the Serb lines), in order to have him responsible for several murders in Srebrenica -- to have his responsibility for several murders in Srebrenica established. I know his case very well. The commander, Rasim Delic, charged me with deciding whether to send him back or try him here, since there was substantial evidence that he had been implicated in several murders in Srebrenica. We discussed this for a long time and finally decided that his potential crimes do not fall under the statute of limitations, that he would be held responsible for them sooner or later, and that the priority at that time was to send him back to Srebrenica. I thank God that he was sent back since he led the breakthrough from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, I have a question in connection with this. Did you talk to Mr. Oric as to how it came to have him return from Tuzla to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric organised his return by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this Mr. Golic tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I visited him when he was involved in an accident, when a helicopter was taken down. That was several days later.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the same helicopter that Mr. Delic had organised for his arrival?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please allow me to finish my question. Was that the same helicopter that Mr. Delic had organised in Tuzla to facilitate the Golic's return to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another question in connection with this: If someone were to claim that Naser Oric decided not to have Ejub Golic prosecuted for the alleged criminal offences, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That would not be true at all. Naser did whatever he could on his part.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document will become D8 -- 859. D859. It doesn't have an ERN number. It consists of eight pages in B/C/S, and five pages in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I need a further 15 minutes, not more, but I wonder if this would be an appropriate time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a break now of 30 minutes and then we will resume soon after. --- Break taken at 4.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry for keeping you waiting but a break means time for others to come to your Chambers with more work and new drafts and problems. So that's how I spent the last 40 minutes. Let's continue and finish, Madam Vidovic, and then Mr. Di Fazio can start.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the course of your testimony you stated that you knew Ejub Golic very well. According to your knowledge of him, did he, in the course of 1992 or later, during the war, ever have the position of deputy commander or commander of the group in Biljecevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Golic was always a leader of the group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Cizmici. He was never a deputy. He was always the leader of his fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript should be corrected. The witness always stated that he was always the leader of his Glogova men rather than fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I hear you well, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I stated, Glogovac -- Glogova men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be shown another document? This is a document by the command of the unit 6338 from Potocari dated 19 May 1993. With the heading "war crime" allegedly signed by the assistant commander for security, Sidik Ademovic. Your Honours, I wish to state the following for the record in relation to this document. This document was delivered to us in three different versions. One of them was here when Mr. Rasim Manas testified. It was P357. However, later on from the OTP we learned that they no longer have this document on their list. Whatever the case, we were delivered the document on several occasions in several different versions and I wish the witness to look at the document and comment upon it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this document. Do you have in front of you a document bearing the stamp "Yugoslavia Belgrade Law Centre"? Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about the law project centre in Belgrade? And how did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the law project centre, which is the co-author of the report on Srebrenica, which stated that with the fall of Srebrenica in 1995, only 1.500 to 2.000 people had been killed. This report was condemned by the major part of the international public. I believe this document is well known.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will quote from this document. It is stated here, "Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, command post 6338, strictly confidential number 06-08/95, Potocari, 19 May, 1993, security organ, war crime." And this is the way this event is described. "In the course of my work in the field, as assistant commander for security of the 280th Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade during extensive investigations into a wide array of issues falling within the scope of security, I have come across information and exact circumstances relating to the death of Milko Markovic, father's name Jovo Markovic from Susnjari. Namely after Arkan's men had left Srebrenica and Goran Zekic, when the Serbs fled, that is left the town, among those who remained in the town of Srebrenica was Markovic. The letter was in his apartment in Srebrenica where he was always intoxicated and repeatedly fired from his weapon. At that time, the army entered Srebrenica and on orders from ex-Veliki the above mentioned was captured and delivered to Mes [phoen]. He was taken across a place, mistreated, prodded a little with a knife, and when he was brought to a brook where his throat was partially slit, he was -- a fire was set and he was left to gradually burn." My question is as follows: Are you the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an apparent forgery. To me, as a professional, these are ludicrous statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an incident involving Milko Markovic, son of Jovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I heard about this matter for the first time -- or rather I learnt about this matter for the first time from the Belgrade press. This is a pure fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the reference number for this document 06-08/95. Do you agree this is a reference number dating from 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that the document bears the date of the 19th of May 1993? You are a policeman. According to the -- to your -- the practice in our parts, is it possible for a document to be dated 1993 and to bear a reference number 95 or should it bear in the reference number the same date as that in which the document was produced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to what I see from the document, this is in contradiction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In May 1993, did you have a stamp with a lily at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the documents bearing a stamp with lilies appeared in your parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In early 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P31? I wish us to compare this document with the present one. P31 is a document by the staff of the Supreme Court of Sarajevo dated 1st January 1994, an order concerning organisational changes-establishment. Under D, the 280th Light East Bosnian Brigade should be set up with the establishment number T31327. Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this document indicates that the order for the formation of the 282nd Brigade came from Sarajevo only on the 1st of January 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is an apparent contradiction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, then, that it arrived only on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that part of this order is also unit 6338?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at this document bearing the date 15th of May 1993, the earlier document, which was apparently signed by you, the command unit 6338, strictly confidential and so on. Do you agree with me that according to this document, you were the assistant commander with the 280th Brigade on the 19th of May 1993 and that the unit bears the number 6338?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says. However, I was not a member of any specific unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that on the 19th of May 1993, you would have had to be a prophet, clairvoyant, to draw upon the name or a number of a unit which did not exist in 1993 and which was established by an order issued a year later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, in this period, on the 19th of May 1993, did you hold the rank of a captain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was much later, much, much later, that I was given a rank, upon arrival in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell the Trial Chamber, what were your whereabouts in 1993, in May 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to tell the Trial Chamber that at the end of 1992, and I mean December 1992, January, February, and March 1993, there were intense fights in my area and I suffered from chilblains that I still have in my hands and feet, and on the 7th of May 1993, I was in the hospital. I was severely ill. I was -- I underwent a surgery that I hardly survived.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
